title: Those who repent and obey in true faith may be secure of God’s mercy and of remitted sins
source_text: IV. Sed quod attinet ad eos qui seria peccati poenitentia ducti ad Dei clementiam in Christo confugiunt, & Christi praeceptis ex vera fide, & animo syncero obtemperare student, existimamus eos securos esse posse de Dei erga se misericordia, & certo confidere sibi esse remissa peccata: adeoque sanctitatem & justitiam illam quam sectantur, & cui assiduam operam navant, ad vitam aeternam Deo acceptam esse.
pass_a_gloss: But as for those who, led by serious repentance for sin, flee to God’s clemency in Christ and from true faith and a sincere mind strive to obey Christ’s precepts, we judge that they can be secure concerning God’s mercy toward them and can certainly trust that their sins have been remitted to them: and therefore that the holiness and righteousness which they pursue, and to which they give diligent labor, is accepted by God unto eternal life.
pass_b_english: Serious penitents who trust Christ and obey him may be secure of mercy and remitted sins.
The holiness they pursue is accepted by God unto eternal life.
